entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The present petition has been filed with the allegation that the respondent No.5/PWD is constructing a load on the private land of the petitioner in Survey No.636/1/2(S).
Counsel for petitioner contended that a new road project has been sanctioned in the name of Manpur Bypass.
However, the location of some portions of the old road has been changed and now some portion of the road is passing through the private land of the petitioner.
It is further alleged that the respondents have already placed murrum and other construction material to construct the said road on the private land of the petitioner unauthorizedly.

Per contra, counsel for the respondents contended that the petitioner raises dispute questions of fact whether the petitioner is owner of the land, whether the road is indeed being constructed on the private land of the petitioner or on the public land etc.
Upon hearing learned counsel for parties, it is evident that the contentions raised by the petitioner are in the realm of the facts.
It requires to be established whether the road is being constructed through the private land of the petitioner and whether the petitioner is indeed the owner of the land.
Petitioner has already filed a detailed representation before the Collector vide Annexure P-5 dated 30.05.2024 which is said to be pending consideration before the Collector.

In view of the above, this petition is disposed off directing the respondent No.2/Collector, District Umaria to take up and decide the representation submitted by the petitioner within a period of 10 days from the production of the certified copy of the order passed today.

In case, it is found that the road is indeed being constructed through the 3 WP-16158-2024 private land of the petitioner without acquisition, then the Collector shall be well advised to initiate appropriate proceedings under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
